questions.q: What does the Apex Jobs page in Setup display?
options: Every future method invocation, Queueable job, and Batch Apex run, with status and progress
Only Scheduled Apex jobs and their next fire times
A list of every Apex class deployed to the org
User login history for the past 30 days
questions.explain: The Apex Jobs page in Setup lists future method invocations, Queueable jobs, and Batch Apex runs, along with status, submitted time, errors, and (for Batch Apex) progress.

questions.q: What object underlies both the Apex Jobs Setup page and SOQL queries that check on future, Queueable, and Batch Apex job status?
options: CronTrigger
AsyncApexJob
ApexLog
SetupAuditTrail
questions.explain: AsyncApexJob is the queryable system object underlying the Apex Jobs page, with fields like Status, JobType, NumberOfErrors, TotalJobItems, and JobItemsProcessed.

questions.q: Which two objects would you query to check a Scheduled Apex job's next run time and status, the SOQL equivalent of the Scheduled Jobs Setup page?
options: AsyncApexJob and ApexClass
CronTrigger and CronJobDetail
ApexJob and ApexSchedule
ScheduledApexJob and ApexTrigger
questions.explain: A scheduled job registered with System.schedule appears as a CronTrigger record, linked to a CronJobDetail record holding the job's name — together the queryable equivalent of the Scheduled Jobs Setup page.

questions.q: A Batch Apex job's AsyncApexJob record shows Status = 'Completed' but NumberOfErrors = 3. What does this actually mean?
options: The job failed entirely and no records were processed
The job as a whole finished, but three of its chunks hit an unhandled exception — meaning part of the data wasn't actually processed successfully
NumberOfErrors always shows 0 for a Completed job, so this combination is impossible
Completed with errors means the job will automatically retry those chunks
questions.explain: A Completed status with a nonzero NumberOfErrors means some chunks succeeded and the job overall finished running, but specific chunks failed with unhandled exceptions — a Completed status alone doesn't guarantee every record was processed.

questions.q: Why is it worth monitoring AsyncApexJob and CronTrigger regularly, rather than only when something visibly breaks?
options: Because failure modes like partial batch errors or a silently-stopped scheduled job don't necessarily produce an obvious, visible error elsewhere
Monitoring isn't actually necessary once a job has been deployed successfully once
AsyncApexJob records are automatically deleted after 24 hours, so there's nothing to monitor
Because Setup pages are the only way to view this data — SOQL cannot query these objects
questions.explain: Real failure modes — partial batch errors masked by an overall Completed status, or a scheduled job that silently stopped firing — don't necessarily surface as an obvious visible error, which is exactly why regular monitoring catches problems that the absence of an error wouldn't.
